description: Wildfire Predictive Services is an open-source code base published by the Government of British Columbia to support decision making in wildfire prevention, preparedness, response and recovery. The repository holds a Python back end (an API built with uv and using GDAL, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, and Redis) and a JavaScript web front end, with setup documentation per component; the project marks itself as stable. Coverage: built for British Columbia's wildfire service; the individual tools and models inside were not read beyond the README. Format and access: source code on GitHub; native setup is the supported way to run it, and the Docker Compose and dev container set-ups are marked as currently unsupported. Licence: Apache 2.0, read from the repository licence file. Caveats: the applications depend on the province's internal data feeds, so running them elsewhere needs other weather and fire data; the software was not run for this record. Simulation uses: an example of an operational wildfire decision support stack whose components can be reused for emergency response and wildfire hazard exposure studies of infrastructure. Related records: WRF-SFIRE (model-openwfm-wrf-sfire-coupled-weather-fire) is a coupled weather and fire spread model.
